text:
linda_m: Quick sync — post-launch patching plan idea: run a 10-working-day "rapid patch" window focusing exclusively on crashers, SLA regressions, and data-loss. Non-blocking UX requests go to a "follow-on" grooming board.

tony_r: +1. Suggest we define a "customer-impact score" (CIS) = users_affected * severity_weight * recency_factor. Anything CIS > 100 => top priority.

kevin_s: Can we tie CIS to customer tier? e.g., BoltMed weight x3. Also need to estimate dev+infra delta per fix.

linda_m: Yep. I'll run a quick script to map recent errors to customers and surface the ones with highest CIS. Will post CSV.

product_lead: Two guardrails: 1) feature freeze for the patch window (no non-security feature merges), 2) any patch must include a test that reproduces the issue in CI and a rollback plan. Owners must be named and 24h on-call during patch window.

tony_r: For rollout: start with internal canary (qa + staging), then 2% prod for 1h, then 10% for 4h. Rollback triggers: spike in error_count > 40% or token_cost increase > 2x. I'll write quick runbook snippet.

ops_bot: Note: deploy approvals still need runbook signoff + #eng-oncall tag. See `deploy-bot` flow.

kevin_s: We should also mark any fix that increases infra by >10% for PM review. Some caching fixes might do that. I'll add `infra_delta` to tickets.

linda_m: Action items: 1) I publish CIS-ranked CSV by EOD. 2) Tony drafts runbook + canary thresholds. 3) Kevin adds infra estimates. 4) Product to confirm 10-day window and owners by tomorrow noon. If ok, start Monday.

product_lead: Fine. Approving 10-day rapid patch. Thanks 555 let's keep communication tight in #product-status and ping me for any customer escalations.

linda_m: will do. :white_check_mark:
